title: Regional latency envelope and staged cutover criteria for inference runtime migration
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
PRD snapshot: We are migrating a subset of hosted inference traffic from runtime-1.x (legacy kernel selection and batching) to runtime-2.1 (adaptive kernel selection + prefix KV cache improvements). This ticket defines the per-region latency envelopes, availability targets, error-budget definitions, and automated staged cutover gates required for an operational canary and subsequent ramp to 100% regional traffic.

Problem: Early experiments showed p99 regression in certain edge cases (multi-tenant short prompts) after enabling the new allocator. Without well-defined per-region envelopes and automated rollback gates we risk customer-visible latency and SLA breaches during ramp.

Goal: Provide a precise, measurable rulebook so SRE/Infra/Runtime and Product can conduct safe regional cutovers with automated safety nets and clear post-cutover acceptance criteria. This PRD focuses on hosted API regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) and excludes Dedicated/Private rollout plans (handled in separate PM ticket).

Scope (in):
- Per-region p50/p95/p99 latency envelopes for text-generation and chat streaming first-byte/first-token metrics.
- Regional availability targets and error budgets (definition and burn rules).
- Canary plan: tenant-weighted canary, ramp schedule, minimum diagnostics per tenant.
- Automated gates for pause/rollback based on burn-rate and absolute threshold breaches.
- Observability & contract tests required pre-cutover.

Scope (out):
- Dedicated capacity SLA changes.
- Model-specific precision SLOs for quantized variants (refer to PM-15937).

Stakeholders: Product (Ayesha Kapoor), Runtime/Infra (Liam O'Connor, Mei Chen), SRE (Diego Marquez), Console/Observability (Priya Nair), Support (Jordan Blake).

Timeline: Canary start window: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-15; full regional ramp target completion by 2026-03-31.

Notes: This ticket supersedes the ad-hoc canary checklist used last quarter; aim is to automate gating in the release pipeline and to ensure consistent telemetry across regions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-region latency envelopes defined and encoded in the release config: us-east-1 p50<=60ms, p95<=220ms, p99<=450ms for text-gen 128-token median workload
eu-west-1 p50<=70ms, p95<=240ms, p99<=520ms; ap-southeast-1 p50<=80ms, p95<=300ms, p99<=650ms
Regional availability (5xx+error rate) must be >=99.9% for the 72-hour post-ramp window; any region below 99.5% triggers automatic rollback to previous runtime variant

Error budget definition: rolling 7-day error budget per region set to 0.1% of requests (equivalent to 99.9% availability); automated burn detection defined as 3x historic burn rate over a 15-minute sliding window
Canary tenant set validated: minimum 12 tenants per region covering small, medium, and heavy qps profiles; telemetry dashboard shows per-tenant p95 and error-rate trends before ramp
Canary ramp schedule enforced in pipeline: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% regional traffic with minimum 30m observation at each step and conditional pass criteria
Automated rollback gates implemented: immediate rollback on absolute p99 > 2x envelope for 10 continuous minutes, or error-rate > 1% for 5 continuous minutes
Burn-rate gate implemented: if burn-rate > 3x expected for 30 minutes, pause ramp and alert SRE + Product oncall

Observability: dashboards (latency percentiles, error-rate, success-by-tenancy, model-fallbacks) and trace sampling (1:100) enabled for canary tenants; contract-tests must pass in staging against representative prompt sets
Post-cutover validation job runs for 72 hours and produces a pass/fail artifact (SLO report) stored in Confluence and linked to the release ticket
Runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and emergency mitigation (circuit-breaker thresholds, manual tenant shunt) and reviewed by SRE and Support

decisions: Tenant-weighted canary chosen over single-tenant needle to get representative telemetry across tail behaviors.
Use 15-minute sliding window for burn-rate detection and 30-minute action window for sustained anomalies before auto-pause.
Fallback behavior: automatically switch routed traffic in-region to runtime-1.x if rollback gate trips; also open an incident and tag the release.
Telemetry retention and redaction policy updated for canary traces to meet security guidance (no raw prompt persist beyond 48 hours).
